From: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org> To: "Theodore Ts'o" <tytso@mit.edu> Cc: Linux Kernel Developers List < linux-kernel@vger.kernel.org >, Ext4 Developers List < linux-ext4@vger.kernel.org > Subject: Re: [GIT PULL] updates for 7.4-rc5 Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 12:36:19 -0800 [thread overview] Message-ID: <CAHk-=whyUfwzMDMTpih8Xs1MxmhwTCDAc_YwUSZG79vXFMLU=Q@mail.gmail.com> ( raw ) In-Reply-To: < awW86EI5fYafQx-o@mit.edu > On Tue, 24 Nov 2026 at 08:36, Theodore Ts'o <tytso@mit.edu> wrote: > > The bulk of the new lines was caused by adding KUnit tests, which > makes it safer to validate AI generated patches. Honestly, I don't think this was appropriate for this stage. You should have kept your tests in a separate branch for your testing, and done this *huge* update for the next merge window. This whole notion of "anything that is a fix goes in -rc" is bogus. I've taken this, despite serious reservations and some bad conflicts due to this braindamage. But next time this kind of sh*t happens I'll just ignore it. STOP THINKING THAT YOU - OR AI - NEVER ADD BUGS WHEN YOU FIX SOMETHING. There's a why we have release candidates and several weeks of calming things down. Yes, I'm pissed off. Why the hell people have such a hard time understanding such a simple concept is hard to understand. If you think that "41197 insertions" is ok and cannot introduce new problems just because most of it won't be compiled or becasue they were fixes for other things, you are full of crap. If the bugs were subtle things that have been around for a while without being detected by AI, the fixes by definition are fixing something subtle and rare that nobody has noticed until now. And that makes the *fixes* possibly buggy. I was going to just unpull it, but I dealt with this and am giving you a fair warning instead. Get your shit together and stop this kind of idiocy. And tell your AI companion to get its act together, and do any new development and test-cases ON A SEPARATE DAMN BRANCH, so that it can be merged during the MERGE WINDOW. What's so hard to understand about this? And yes, it will mean that *you* have to deal with the resulting conflicts while running those tests, but dammit, it will also mean that we don't introduce tens of thousands od lines of random crap in the middle of a release! Linus
